title: Sandboxes, scratch orgs, environments, and development models
objectives: Define a scratch org as a source-driven disposable deployment of code and metadata with a maximum 30-day life.
Define sandboxes as copies of a Salesforce org for development, testing, and training without compromising production.
Choose scratch org versus sandbox versus production as environments, including source tracking defaults.
Contrast org development (unpackaged source to sandboxes) with package development (versioned packages) without turning this lesson into a packaging deep-dive.
diagnostic_question: A new hire wants a place to build LAB_ Apex. Do you spin a scratch org, clone a developer sandbox, or open production? What expires, what copies data, and what stays source-driven?
definition: A scratch org is a source-driven and disposable deployment of Salesforce code and metadata, configured from a definition file or org shape, lasting at most 30 days (default 7). Sandboxes are copies of your Salesforce org used for development, testing, and training without compromising production. Environments are those orgs plus production. Development models describe whether you promote unpackaged source through sandboxes (org development) or version packages (package development). ([Scratch Orgs](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_scratch_orgs.htm); [Sandboxes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_sandboxes.htm); [Continuous Integration](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_ci.htm))
why_it_matters: Building in production is not an environment strategy. Treating a scratch org like a durable UAT sandbox loses work at expiration. Interviewers want disposable versus copied, metadata versus data copy, and org model versus package model as separate choices.
sixty_second_explanation: Think of film production lots. A scratch org is a soundstage built from a script (definition file), empty of last year's extras, torn down within 30 days. A sandbox is a standing backlot copied from the studio; some lots copy sets only, some copy extras. Production is opening night. Org development hauls unpackaged sets from lot to lot. Package development ships numbered containers of sets (DEVOPS-005). Never store personal extras on the soundstage.
deeper_explanation: Scratch orgs are source-driven and disposable deployments of code and metadata. They emulate editions via a shared definition file. You can install packages and deploy synthetic or dummy data. Do not add personal data. Use them to start a project or feature branch, test, automate, or start from scratch. They have a maximum 30-day lifespan, selectable 1–30 days, default 7; after expiration they cannot be restored. Source tracking is enabled by default; you can disable it for CI that only creates, deploys, tests, and deletes. Scratch orgs start empty of much sample metadata found in Developer Edition sign-ups. They require a Dev Hub. ([Scratch Orgs](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_scratch_orgs.htm))

Sandboxes are copies of your Salesforce org for development, testing, and training without compromising production data and applications. Salesforce CLI can create, clone, or refresh them from a sandbox definition file. Refresh brings latest metadata and sometimes data from the source org—Needs verification of which sandbox types copy which data volumes against current Help. Sandboxes traditionally live longer than scratch orgs and are the usual UAT and training environments. ([Sandboxes](https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.sfdx_dev.meta/sfdx_dev/sfdx_dev_sandboxes.htm))

Source tracking is on by default for scratch and sandbox orgs and never for production (DEVOPS-002). CI that only boots a scratch org, deploys, tests, and deletes often disables tracking for speed. Personal data must not go into scratch orgs; sandbox data copies can still contain PII and need governance.

Salesforce DX CI documentation provides sample repos for an org development model and a package development model. Org development typically deploys unpackaged project source through sandbox environments. Package development uses versioned unlocked or managed packages as the unit (details in DEVOPS-005). Do not treat 'we have sandboxes' as proof you chose a model.

mental_model.analogy: Film lots: scratch org = script-built soundstage that is struck within 30 days; sandbox = standing backlot copied from the studio; production = opening night; org model = moving unpackaged sets; package model = numbered shipping containers of sets.

Org shape and snapshots are extra scratch creation methods, not film extras.
Package install in a scratch org is not the same as choosing the package development model for production.

interview_explanation.thirty_seconds: Scratch orgs are disposable source-driven metadata environments that expire in at most 30 days. Sandboxes are copies of the org for test and training. Production is not a playground. Org versus package development is how you promote, not which lot you booked.
interview_explanation.two_minutes: I match the job: feature/CI → scratch from a definition file, no PII, Git is truth because the org will vanish. UAT/training/prod-like data → sandbox, with refresh and PII rules. I never develop in production. I name org development as unpackaged deploys through sandboxes and package development as versioned packages. I do not quote unofficial sandbox storage numbers.

interview_questions.question: Scratch org versus sandbox?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A scratch org is a disposable source-driven metadata environment that lasts at most 30 days. A sandbox is a copied org for development, testing, and training without harming production.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I do not call scratch a sandbox type. Scratch starts empty of much DE sample metadata, uses a definition file, forbids personal data, and cannot be restored after expiry. Sandboxes can be created, cloned, or refreshed and are the durable UAT/training choice. Production is neither.
interview_questions.example: Feature branch → 7-day scratch. Two-month training → sandbox.
tradeoffs: Clean empty org versus prod-like data

interview_questions.question: What is the scratch org expiration policy?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: You pick 1 to 30 days, default 7. After expiration the org is deleted and cannot be restored. That is why Git is truth.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Expiration is a feature: sync often. Deleting a scratch org does not end the subscription; creating a new one counts against limits—Needs verification of current daily/active numbers for the Dev Hub edition. I never promise Support will undelete it.
interview_questions.example: A 7-day scratch used for LAB_ work; class survives only because it was committed.
weak_answer_warnings: They last until you log out

interview_questions.question: CI needs a fresh org every pipeline run. What do you provision?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: A scratch org, often with source tracking off, deploy from Git, run tests, delete. No personal data.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: The scratch guide lists this CI pattern. Tracking slows jobs that will never pull Setup clicks. I still use a definition file so features match. If tests need data, I import synthetic fixtures, not production extracts. Long-running UAT stays on a sandbox.
interview_questions.example: Jenkins job: org create scratch --no-track-source, deploy force-app, apex run test, org delete.
tradeoffs: Scratch spin-up time versus sandbox reuse
weak_answer_warnings: Full sandbox per CI run as the default

interview_questions.question: A developer built for a week only in a scratch org and never retrieved. It expired. What failed?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Source-driven discipline failed. Scratch orgs are unrestorable. The metadata should have been in Git.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I treat this as a process incident, not a platform bug. We reconstruct from memory only as a last resort and then immediately retrieve/commit. I add a checklist: daily status clean and pushed. I do not ask Support to restore the scratch org.
interview_questions.example: Expired scratch; LAB_ Flow only existed there; team rebuilds from screenshots then commits.
tradeoffs: Daily retrieve overhead versus catastrophic loss
Scratch vs sandbox for click-heavy admins
follow_ups: Would a sandbox have saved them?
How do you detect unpushed work?

interview_questions.question: Org development model versus package development model?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Org model promotes unpackaged Git source through environments. Package model versions unlocked or managed packages as the unit. DX even ships CI samples for both.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: force-app as a folder is not proof of packaging. I ask how production receives change: source deploy, change set, or package install. Unlocked packages are the usual internal package model (next lesson). I do not pretend one model is always faster without evidence.
interview_questions.example: Team A deploys force-app to UAT sandbox. Team B installs unlocked package version 1.2.3.
tradeoffs: Simple source deploy versus versioned install/rollback story

interview_questions.question: Why do scratch orgs exist if sandboxes already exist?
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Scratch orgs give a repeatable empty-enough org from a definition file, aligned to Git, without copying production PII, and they go away.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: Sandboxes copy an org and are right for prod-like tests. Scratch orgs optimize developer and CI inner loops. They are created on sandbox instances but are not sandbox types. I mention source tracking defaults and Dev Hub as the permit office.
interview_questions.example: Same project-scratch-def.json on every laptop so Lightning features match.
tradeoffs: Dev Hub limits vs sandbox licenses

interview_questions.question: Scratch org missing a custom object that production has, after deploy of only new Apex.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Scratch starts empty of much sample and production metadata. You must deploy the objects the Apex depends on, or use a fuller source set, or choose a sandbox copy.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: This is a shape problem. The definition file does not copy production objects. Org-dependent unlocked packages exist because unpackaged org metadata may be missing—that is the next topic. I do not blame the Apex compiler first.
interview_questions.example: LAB_GateService references LAB_Gate__c which was never in the scratch payload.

interview_questions.question: Design environments for a 12-person team with CI, UAT, and production.
interview_questions.answer_30_seconds: Git is truth. CI scratch orgs. Developer scratch or short sandboxes. Durable UAT sandbox. Production locked. No PII in scratch. Apex never authored in production.
interview_questions.answer_2_minutes: I draw lots: soundstages for CI/dev, backlot for UAT, opening night for prod. I name the promotion model. I put definition files in Git. I call out refresh PII. I do not invent sandbox refresh calendars. I keep packaging as a fork in the road, not a detour that skips environments.
interview_questions.example: dev scratch + CI scratch + UAT partial/full sandbox per license + prod.
